Tyrone Mings defends well but he cannot prevent Galatasaray winning another second-half corner.

Galatasaray with a double change: Sara and Ugochukwu on for Batrakov and Lemina.

Emery responds in kind: Hemmings and Barkley on for Manzambi and McGinn.

Aston Villa struggling to find any rhythm after another stoppage in the game, but Galatasaray are enjoying more of the territory. Nicolas Jackson has been a revelation this season but has been underwhelming in the second half.

Now Gortetzka is waved on by the referee, who made Villa wait because Gomes took too long to walk off the pitch. Suzuki commands his box in the air once again to climb a high ball launched into the mixer.

Alysson and Gomes are the players coming off for Mbaye and Goretzka, but the German midfielder has been to wait on the touchline by the referee much to Emery’s Fury. Gomes has already gone off, so Villa are down to 10. Bizarre officiating, not sure I can recall seeing that.

Now Galatasaray have a corner! But Villa clear at the near post.

Villa floundering and under pressure for the first time in the game, Mbaye and Goretzka are about to be introduced by Emery.

Galatasaray have a free-kick in a crossing position left of centre, but Akgun’s delivery floated over everyone in the box and Torreira is then penalised for a foul on Manzambi.

Galatasaray have made a change in their attack, with a more orthodox striker in Gul replaces Elmali, so Yilmaz moves out to the left. Torreira wins a foul in midfield, but Gomes and Kamara were convinced they had won the ball cleanly.

That aggro has given Galatasaray a lift and the noise is now increasing.

Villa have slightly lost their way in the last 10 minutes, they are not passing the ball with their early fluency and appear caught between holding what they have or pushing on for a goal. Maatsen the latest player guilty of a cheap giveaway.

Akgun reacts with fury after he is tripped on the sly by Alysson to stop a break away, and they square up to each other. Both players have been booked, so there have been five yellow cards so far.

Suzuki does well to claim a cross but he caught Elmali who stays down in the penalty area to receive some treatment. A little bit of needle in the game is welcome because neither team is creating much.

Galatasaray waste a corner, and then Villa spring a counter-attack despite Maatsen’s initial poor pass. Sanchez crashed into a challenge on Alysson, before McGinn returns the favour with interest on Batrakov. McGinn is booked for the tackle, Batrakov for his reaction. The Galatasaray player kicked out slightly after he was bodied by the Villa man. Both benches were up, but no further punishement for either player.

Jackson nods the ball down into a dangerous area but Bardakci clears for Galatasaray. Villa continue to dominate possession, Galatasaray keep going long towards Yilmaz to no avail. They are feeling the absence of Osimhen.

Very messy defending from Galatasaray and there are vociferous appeals for a Villa penalty after a lunging challenge in the box, but the referee and VAR decide there is nothing in it. The layer of sand under the top surface of the pitch is becoming increasingly visible as the game goes on.

No changes from either manager at half-time.

Unai Emery will be fairly satisfied with that first-half performance.

In a match of few chances, Villa have frustrated the home team and defended resolutely in the rare occasions Galatasaray have applied pressure.

The pitch is slowing the game down which is helping Villa. There was a weird booking for Nicolas Jackson late in the half so it would be no surprise to see him taken off by Emery either at half-time or very early in the second.

A controlled and composed 45 minutes from Villa, but in truth Galatasaray have put them under very little pressure. McGinn, Manzambi and Jackson have produced some smooth flicks and touches, but there has been a lack of devastation in the final third. That has been the missing element for Villa so far. For all the talk of the atmosphere, they should be beating this team.

Nicolas Jackson has been booked, and Alysson loses the ball cheaply to put Galatasaray away on the counter-attack. Mings is up early to head the corner away. The home team continue to look pretty toothless.

Elmali’s cross from the Galatasaray left is woefully overhit and Suzuki claims, but it was a poor pass from Harwood-Bellis that instigated the attack. Villa soon restore order with a spell of possession.

Unsurprisingly, the best pass of the match so far has come from Zion Suzuki.

The Villa goalkeeper has just pinged a pearler over 40 odd yards to Alysson on the right wing.

Galatasaray find some joy with quick switches of play with Villa’s defensive shape quite narrow, but Akgun’s chipped cross was overhit.

Joao Gomes then takes an extra touch inside his own box, but moves the ball on before he is caught in possession.

Torreira than clatters Gomes, not his first foul on the night, but somehow he escapes a booking.

McGinn is picking up some midfield positions that are hard for Galatasaray to pick up, but a couple of Hollywood passes from there have not come off.

Better attacking play from the home team, but Mings was well positioned to head clear a deflected cross.

Villa with another slick move, and this one had more attacking punch at the end of it. Maatsen delivered a wicked low cross and Manzambi was waiting for a tap-in but Sanchez made a last-ditch challenge. No doubt that Villa are the better team.

For a moment it looks as if Manzambi had missed a glorious chance but the flag belatedly went up for offside against Jackson who collected the ball wide right when well ahead of the play.

Villa are doing a very good job of frustrating both the Galatasaray players and their supporters so far.

They are slowing the game down and producing some neat interplay in advanced positions.

Johan Manzambi, in particular, is covering a lot of ground.

Suzuku rushes off his line to sweep up a through ball, but Alysson had also tracked a run all the way. Singo passes forward quickly but Galatasaray’s playmaker Batrakov cannot put the ball under his spell.

John McGinn with a chance to deliver a free-kick from a crossing position, but Galatasaray win the header at the back post. Villa continue to be comfortable in the game, without really working the goalkeeper Cakir. The home crowd are restless, Galatasaray have yet to muster a menacing attacking.

Villa moving the ball well inside Galatasaray’s half with some neat interplay between Manzambi and Jackson when they are in close proximity, but there is no telling pass or shot at the end of the move.

Lovely turn from John McGinn between the lines but Galatasaray’s defender Bardakci intercepted his through ball. Manzambi started wide left on the team sheet, but Maatsen’s runs forward are allowing the Swiss to play in a narrower position.

Akgun wins a free-kick for Galatasaray, who have grown into the contest in the last few minutes. Torreira and Batrakov swapping positions in midfield, and Singo is an impressive player at right-back. The delivery from the free-kick is poor though.

Galatasaray did beat Liverpool twice in this competition last season so cannot be taken lightly tonight.

The pitch does appear to be cutting up a bit in some areas already.

Jackson perhaps unfortunate not be awarded a foul in the left corner, but this has been a bright start by Villa.

Their front players Manazmbi, Alysson and Jackson all combined in a one-touch move after Suzuki played long before the Villa striker was flagged offside.

Lovely pass from Zion Suzuki inside the opening minute, picking out Harwood-Bellis who was free down the right. He found Manzambi unmarked in the middle before Maatsen’s progress down the left was halted. Villa enjoy drawing a press, so it could suit them if the home team are aggressive.

Villa get the game under way, and from the aerial view you can see the seams between patches of the pitch.

A cacophony of hoots, howls and whistles will greet the Villa players, and the same will be true of their every touch of the ball. Aleksey Batrakov, likely to play in behind Yilmaz for the home team, has been identified as Galatasaray’s potential danger man.

Alejandro Garnacho has now been left out of the Villa squad for four games in a row.

He trained at Bodymoor Heath on Monday so does not appear to be injured.

It is looking pretty bleak for the Chelsea loanee, and the comparisons with Liverpool’s Harvey Elliott last season are impossible to escape.

Villa have made a solid start on their return to the Champions League, winning three and losing one.

Victory here would give them a fine chance of progress to the knock-out stages, and provide Unai Emery with some insurance.

Villa face a daunting pair of home games against Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund in their next two league phase matches.

No problems, no. We must play in all pitches, even synthetic we play in the Champions League. It’s not perfect but it is good enough to play football.

Very competitive [on Galatasaray], they are at home so, so intense with their supporters.

We must play focused, together, try and set our game plan as much as possible. We must try and dominate in the way we must build the team.

Six months after the glory of winning the Europa League final in Istanbul, Aston Villa are back on the banks of the Bosphorus.

A potentially tricky match awaits against the Turkish champions, with much of the pre-match scrutiny on the state of the pitch.

Villa were unable to train on Rams Park on Monday as the club is undertaking repair work to the surface.

A positive result and no injuries would represent a great evening for Unai Emery.

Emery appears to be using the versatile Manzambi in a wide left starting position with McGinn in the middle in front of Gomes and Kamara. Mings for Pau Torres is surely all about rotation, with Villa going to Ipswich on Tuesday night. Harwood-Bellis could play at right-back in a similar set-up to the one Villa deployed at Old Trafford.

Lucas Torreira was signed by Arsenal in 2018, Unai Emery’s first summer as head coach. Gundogan has not played many minutes at all this season, but is back on the bench. Osimhen and Leao missing a significant chunk of the season is a major disappointment.

Aston Villa supporters have happy memories of Istanbul after May’s Europa League final, and they return to face Galatasaray this evening in a fixture which could forecast their Champions League prospects.

It has been par for the course for Unai Emery’s team in Europe so far, with victories over Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking and a defeat at Barcelona aligning with the form book.

Nine points from 12 leaves them inside the top eight at the halfway stage of the league phase, but tougher challenges are ahead with PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come after tonight’s game.

Since a statement victory over Manchester City, it has been a frustrating time for Villa either side of the international break. They were dumped out of the League Cup by Bournemouth, were second-best in a home draw with Fulham, threw away a pair of two-goal leads at Old Trafford, and were held by Sunderland at the weekend.

Though Villa put six past Galatasaray’s city rivals Fenerbahce at Villa Park, away games against Turkish opposition can be different beasts, as Liverpool discovered in the last round of Champions League matches.

Galatasaray’s two major attacking threats, Victor Osimhen and Rafael Leão, are both absent with injuries. Davinson Sanchez and Lucas Torreira are former Premier League players in their squad. Galatasaray have won two of four Champions League games, losing to Barcelona and Sporting Lisbon, but they are top of the Turkish Super Lig.

Villa will be without right-back Matty Cash owing to a concussion sustained during the international break with Poland, but will hope to have Victor Lindelof available again after he missed the Sunderland draw with illness.

Emery’s team were unable to train at Rams Park yesterday in order to give a troublesome pitch maximum recovery time after emergency renovation work.

“If we could have trained in the stadium of Galatasaray, maybe we would have decided for the same situation, but it’s not changing our routine,” Emery said. “How the pitch is going to be tomorrow is important, but it’s not an excuse because it’s [the same] for both teams. Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible.”

#922. Dengue has exploded globally with shocking speed

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

A pregnant person with dengue speaks to a nurse in Peru, which has been hit by a surge of cases this year. Credit: Juan Carlos Cisneros/AFP/Getty

The debilitating viral disease called dengue has exploded in incidence far more than previously thought, a new analysis suggests.

The number of reported global cases of dengue, which is transmitted by infected mosquitoes, rose from 430,000 in 1990 to 14.7 million in 2024 — a 34-fold increase, the analysis says.

Dengue is spreading in Europe: how worried should we be?

Dengue is spreading in Europe: how worried should we be?

The data were presented on 22 November at the annual meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene (ASTMH) in National Harbor, Maryland. Scientists also provided some of the strongest results yet about a counter-intuitive way to curb the disease’s staggering spread: the release of specially modified mosquitoes. But researchers also presented discouraging data on other solutions, and scientists at the meeting emphasized that the campaign to beat back dengue will be complicated and costly.

“We’re in an extraordinary and pivotal moment” in the history of studying mosquito-borne illnesses, said Albert Ko, president of ASTMH. Trial results presented at the meeting showed, he said, that “we can get rigorous evidence on what works, what doesn’t and what needs to be done to scale these effective interventions to protect the 4 billion people” around the world who are exposed to dengue and other mosquito-borne illnesses.

Dengue causes fever, headaches and severe bone pain. It is transmitted mainly by Aedes aegypti, a species of mosquito that thrives in warm, urban environments. Global warming and increased urbanization have expanded the mosquitoes’ range. Existing vaccines provide imperfect protection.

Cases of dengue are often recorded in disparate databases that aren’t easily comparable, says Ahyoung Lim, an infectious-disease modeler at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, who was involved in the study on dengue incidence. The results have also been published as a preprint1 on Research Square ahead of peer review. This has meant that no single database has captured the total number of reported dengue cases over time, leading Lim and her team to compile the most complete record of reported cases and use statistical modelling tools to fill in gaps in which data were missing.

The staggering increase in reported cases isn’t surprising, says Eng Eong Ooi, a dengue virologist at Duke–NUS Medical School in Singapore who was not involved in the research. Populations in urban environments around the world are steadily increasing, he says, which means that “more and more people are living at risk of dengue each year”.

One promising approach to curb dengue starts with breeding mosquitoes and deliberately infecting them with a bacterium called Wolbachia that reduces the insects’ ability to transmit viruses. When released into the wild, these infected mosquitoes pass the bacterium on to their offspring, eventually lowering the number of highly transmissive mosquitoes.

This is the world’s largest ‘mosquito factory’: its goal is to stop dengue

This is the world’s largest ‘mosquito factory’: its goal is to stop dengue

At the ASTMH meeting, another team of researchers shared results from the first randomized controlled trial in the Americas to test Wolbachia’s effect on dengue transmission. Between January 2021 and May 2022, the researchers released roughly 32 million Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes across designated regions of Brazil and monitored almost 6,000 children living inside and outside these regions. The children provided annual blood samples between 2020 and 2024, and the reseachers found that those in the Wolbachia regions were 68% less likely to be infected with dengue compared with those in non-Wolbachia regions.

These positive results mark an important milestone in proving Wolbachia’s potential to drastically reduce dengue cases, says Elisabeth Nelson, an epidemiologist at the Yale School of Public Health in New Haven, Connecticut, and a researcher on the trial.

Morrison, A. C. et al. Proc. Natl Acad. Sci. USA 119, e2118283119 (2022).

#921. Khawaja 'hurt' by 'personal attacks' from Cummins in sandpaper denials

Usman Khawaja hopes there is collective responsibility for the Sandpapergate scandal in time and says current captain Pat Cummins still has the "opportunity of power"; former batter says Cameron Bancroft feels like a "different person" after finally telling his side of ball-tampering saga

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Usman Khawaja has told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast that he was "hurt" by Pat Cummins' "personal attacks" on him as the Australia Test captain explosively disputed his claims that every member of the side was aware of the use of sandpaper in 2018.

Khawaja made the allegations in his autobiography Sabr and they have since been backed up by David Warner and Cameron Bancroft - two of the players, along with then-skipper Steve Smith, who were slapped with bans following the ball-tampering plot in South Africa.

Cummins, part of the Australia bowling attack on that tour eight years ago, insisted he was not privy to the scheme when he and fellow quicks Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, as well as spinner Nathan Lyon, released a joint-statement in 2021.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

He then categorially denied knowledge earlier this month in a 68-minute press conference in which he accused Khawaja of being "casual" with people's lives.

Khawaja said in a chat with Michael Atherton and Nasser Hussain: "It was the most surprised I've been for a long time. I wasn't expecting that [from Cummins] whatsoever.

"I thought Pat had this really great opportunity to come out and bring everyone together. He's such a great leader. I've said in the book that I love the person he is, love the leader he is, so I thought if anyone can bring us together, it's Pat.

"I had hoped that he would - I text him before, trying do anything I could to make it easier, to do something to bring everyone in - but I realised that wasn't going to happen when he first started talking, so that was really sad.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"Then obviously the personal attacks were sad. I'm not going to lie about that, they hurt from a friend, someone you really respect. That wasn't very Pat Cummins-like, very different to the Pat Cummins I know, and it's hard for me to judge him on that.

"I know Pat, I know his family. They're beautiful, so it was really hard to reconcile the Pat I knew and the Pat that was attacking me personally rather than attacking what I'm saying. That was by far one of the toughest days I've ever experienced.

"I'll caveat that by saying that I have nothing but love for Pat. I don't judge people on certain instances or whatnot. That's not how I live my life. That's not how I function.

"Right now, are we talking? No, not really, but I've still got a lot of hope in my heart that at some stage if there's anyone that can bring everyone together, it's Pat. He's got the opportunity of power, whether it's now or later.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"But I think there was a perfect opportunity there if he took a softer route. He took a real harsh route and I think because of that everything just blew up after that like even more."

Khawaja wanted the team to take collective responsibility for the sandpaper plot at the time but says he was talked out of it by Smith as only the skipper, Warner and Bancroft - the player caught on camera looking to manipulate the ball - were suspended.

The 39-year-old, who retired from international cricket following Australia's 4-1 Ashes thrashing of England last winter, is hopeful "accountability" will eventually come.

He said: "For me it was about the team, Cricket Australia, coming together and saying, 'look, we didn't live up to our standards, we didn't live up to our values and three guys suffered for that'.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"I think there is a way to collectively take this still.

"Will everyone like agree on this? I can't see it happening now the way it's gotten, but for me the middle ground is the collective responsibility and accountability as a team.

"We win together, we lose together, we get caught for ball tampering, we take it together. I think that's achievable, but I can't speak for everyone.

"It doesn't feel there is an ending right now and that sucks for everyone."

Khawaja explained that he became extremely close to Bancroft on the 2019 Ashes tour of England when the latter returned to the side for the first time since 'Sandpapergate' and played what, as things currently stand, are his final two Test matches.

Bancroft's detail-filled, 4,000-word-plus account of the sandpaper deception dropped in the West Australian newspaper on the day of Australia's third ODI against in Hobart, adding even more intrigue to a story that has rocked, and gripped, cricket.

Khawaja said of his relationship with Bancroft: "In the 2019 Ashes, we both played, we got both got dropped and we would play Uno pretty much every day. If I kind of knew him at the start, I knew him really well by the end because we talked about everything.

"I remember asking him about the whole sandpaper incident once, too, He was still working his way through it at the time, trying to figure out how he's dealing with this.

"In his mind I assume he was thinking, 'I'll play 50 more games, become a legend and then I'll earn the respect back of the people'. Unfortunately it didn't work out that way for him and I think that's the thing that's really played on his mind throughout this time.

"I've kept in contact with him periodically. I remember being sat on the bus with him maybe four years ago and I brought this topic up again, asking why he didn't come out and talk about this. He said 'I can't'. He said it to me a few weeks ago actually."

Khawaja continued of Bancroft: "He got in touch with me because he was really struggling. I talked to him on the phone for an hour and a half and told him what I was planning to write in my book.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"That was about halfway during that conversation. The second half of that conversation, I could feel his energy change, because the weight and burden of trying to carry this was eating him up. In his mind, he was thinking, 'no, I'm not the only one here'.

"The first day it came out, he sent me a text saying, 'Uzzy, all I want to say is you've done the right thing and I appreciate this more than you can ever imagine'. That that was one of the things that kept me going because everyone was nailing me that first day.

"We do have a good relationship and a good rapport. He is one of the guys throughout the last two weeks who has been grateful and I needed that, I'm going to be honest, because at times I was like, 'have I done the right thing? Why am I doing this?'

"He finally got to put out a statement. I talked to him afterwards and he's chill, he's laughing, he's joking like he hasn't joked with me in eight years. I can tell that he's a different person.

"If that's the silver lining, it makes it worth it. I can never quite fathom what he went through in those eight years."

#919. Arsenal get the best and worst of Gyokeres on frustrating night for Arteta

Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.

There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came. Even in the 95th minute, Arteta’s players were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League game might have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. By half-time it should have been a formality. Yet, as chance after chance slipped away, there was always a possibility this would end differently.

The leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived. Even so, they did just that and, liberated in the second half, Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser in his team’s best period. There were still 40 minutes for Arsenal to put this one to bed and they found many ways not to do so.

It was notable that the man who put Arsenal ahead in the ninth minute with a right-footed thump from space on the edge of the Dortmund box was the same striker who would miss the best chance to win it. That is the Viktor Gyökeres dilemma. In the space of a single game he can look like a potential match-winner and also the last man his manager would wish to see arriving on the end of a perfect Martin Odegaard cross.

So it proved after 75 minutes when Gyökeres thrust himself at an Odegaard ball into the box that just needed guiding inside a post, yet planted it decisively wide of the mark. On the touchline Arteta tried very hard to hide his despair and failed to do so.

It ended that way, with a heroic defensive performance from the Dortmund defence, including one memorable moment when substitute Serhou Guirassy’s determination to block a cross prompted a double ricochet off his own post. One could make the argument that there were times when it was “unbelievable”, as Arteta later said, that the ball did not find its way in. Although there were also moments when the reasons were self-evident.

“There’s an element of luck,” the Arsenal manager said, “and there is an element of us [not] finishing better.”

In fifth place in the league phase table, dropped points at home do not carry the same jeopardy in the group stage that they once did, yet even so there was a truth for Arteta to chew upon. This is a well-honed, big-game Arsenal Champions League side that he has built. One that reached the final last season and may well go close again, but as ever they seem to be doing so in spite of the great goalscorer that so many of their nearest rivals have at their disposal.

Arteta sounded that warning after defeat in the final in Budapest at the end of May and, while changes have been made, it would be hard to argue that they have been fundamental. This was a good opponent – the leaders of the Bundesliga with many exports from English football who have been reconditioned for the German game. Those include Fábio Silva, Felix Nmecha and Jobe Bellingham, who had a second-half goal narrowly disallowed for offside.

Jobe Bellingham's goal RULED OUT for offside ❌ https://t.co/yaR8EX4Gs3

After a chastening first half in which they found themselves in the teeth of the Arsenal press, Dortmund re-emerged as a much more effective attacking force. They found a way to break the Arsenal press by targeting Christos Tzolis and the run from the teenage French defender Joane Gadou that followed was exceptional. That created the goal for Beier, one of four shots on target from Dortmund – the same number as Arsenal.

Maximilian Beier punishes Arsenal to make it 1-1 😳 https://t.co/OOUmg9JnHo

Dortmund, managed by the West German-born Croat Niko Kovac, did not always have Arsenal’s polish in possession but they certainly had the youth in their legs to match the English champions. In defence their captain Nico Schlotterbeck and Waldemar Anton will not have many better games. They might have been fortunate at times but they will also point to a penalty that was not given, when Gyökeres handled in his own area at the start of the second half.

Gyökeres’s first-half goal was certainly among the best he has scored for the club, invited to shoot by a Dortmund defence that simply stood off as he reached the edge of the area. He will not catch many as full as he did this one. More of a dig than a swish but with the useful consequence of packing a lot of power and a dip that meant goalkeeper Gregor Kobel saw it but could not pick out its flight.

Viktor Gyökeres what a HIT! 👏🔥 https://t.co/5m6FZoE8tQ

Asked about the later Gyökeres miss, Arteta preferred to talk about other aspects of his striker’s performance. “The way he held up the ball, the way he threaded in behind and stretched the pitch,” Arteta said. “There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s the Viktor that we needed.”

Even so, there was some of the Gyökeres the Arsenal manager does not need as early as the end of the first half when he launched a wild shot over from Noni Madueke’s pass. Arteta was without David Raya, who has a shoulder injury and there were no guarantees that he will be back for the Manchester City game on Sunday.

There were some good moments for young Bellingham against Myles Lewis-Skelly in the first half and then a goal disallowed after the break. That came after Beier’s equaliser when Dortmund were at their counter-attacking best. In the final stages, Arsenal pressed hard for the winner and, although there were lots of shots, it would be hard to say there were lots of chances. The one that got away was the one that fell to Gyökeres.

Arteta would later call it “a brilliant performance”. It was hard to shake the feeling from some of the caveats he added that, like everyone else, what he really thought – above all – was that his team should have won.

The performance was superb and there is no question about that from the start to the end. We played against a really good side and the domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more.

I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.

That’s what we want [to finish in the top eight]. We have a big game against Manchester City at home on Sunday so we need to recover really well, we have four days to do that and sustain that momentum the way we are playing and the win will come.

I think these are the best games. I’m really looking forward to it. Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same. We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We’re champions, we’re at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates. There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction.

I feel like the performances from us up until the last shot was incredible at times. Definitely feels like two points dropped like the other day so, having dominated so much of the game we need to take all the points.

I prefer this type of game [more open rather than against a deep defence], there are more breaks and opportunities to attack space. We it’s a low block it’s more about pass, pass, pass and wait for the right moment. I feel like we are well-suited to both types of game.

We could have scored in the second half. We could have won the game in many different ways. We played well and created a lot of chances, we deserved to win the game but sometimes it is like that.

The most important thing is that we create those chances and get shots on goal. For sure we will score goals when games are coming up.

But they are now four points off Real Madrid, who they play next, and more than likely PSG if they beat Roma tomorrow night.

Arsenal with a remarkable combination of poor finishing and bad decision-making in the final third. They ended the night with 56 touches in the Dortmund box and 29 shots, but only four of those shots were on target.

There was time for one late scramble, but at the final whistle it is the Borussia Dortmund fans celebrating the draw.

That result is going to make it very difficult for Arsenal to finish in the top two, but they will hope to have enough for a top-eight finish. They fail to win at home for the first time this season.

Dortmund had their moments, a very strong start to the second half when they could have scored more than once.

But over the piece, the story is Arsenal’s profligacy. Twenty nine shots on goal and more than two expected goals, but not enough to show for it.

Eze with a blocked shot but Arsenal do have Dortmund pushed back in their half for the final 90 seconds. Is there one more chance!

Kobel palms behind Rice’s delivery for another Arsenal corner. Feels like now or never if Arsenal are to find the winner.

Promising attack for Dortmund, but Timber blocked Karestas’s shot.

Then Arsenal go down the other end and win a corner through Hincapie’s persistence.

Gabriel tries to win a header on the edge of Dortmund’s box but gives a foul away. Odegaard’s shot was blocked in the build up, he may have been better off crossing to the back post.

Arsenal with some good football through the lines involving Odegaard and Bruno Guimaraes, but then Konsa was the wrong man in the wrong place and committed a foul. Mikel Merino has replaced Viktor Gyokeres.

Some of the venom has gone out of the Arsenal backlash since the equaliser, but they continue to probe and push numbers forward.

And Declan Rice hits the post! Brilliant slide-rule pass from Eze to release Rice into the box, and his first-time shot with his left foot cannons of the near post.

Dortmund have a throw deep in the Arsenal half now, after Kepa found himself in a tight spot and kicked to touch. Arsenal clear but Eze fails to bring them up the pitch.

Scramble in the Dortmund goal-mouth from an Arsenal free-kick, whipped in low by Odegaard right across the face of goal, kept alive by Hincapie at the back post and the ball bounced off the post when it looked like being an own goal. Kobel stays down to receive some treatment after colliding with the post.

It feels like Arsenal have restored some dominance since the changes, and after some messy play in the penalty box they have a corner. Punched clear by Kobel, before Madueke is fouled.

Arsenal crowd growing a little frustrated with Odegaard for turning down a shot at the edge of the box, and also failing to find Gyokeres with the pass.

Then Gyokeres misses a sitter! Brilliant ball from Odegaard, Gyokeres completely unmarked to meet to inswinging cross but he heads wide from six yards. Hincapie’s run maybe put him off but that would be generous.

Eze with a sloppy giveaway in his own half but Arsenal are not punished, before Rice sets the home team away with some great play in midfield. Eze feeds Gyokeres down the left, but not red player was in the six-yard box for a cross.

Then Madueke cuts inside from the right and shoots not far wide of the near post.

Arsenal’s inability to control this second half has made for a very entertaining game. Two teams going for it. Dortmund seem to accept they can’t defend their way to a result so they might as well try to attack.

Arsenal respond by throwing a couple of punches. First Eze’s shot was deflected over, before Anton made a magnificent block to deny Madueke. The game is swinging back and forth.

Jobe Bellingham wheels away in celebration thinking he has scored for Dortmund after Ryerson’s shot was saved from Kepa but the flag goes up for offside! It took Bellingham ages to realise, and his joy was cut short.

Replays show it was very, very tight indeed. The still image suggested Hincapie was playing him on, but VAR confirms offside as the decision.

To give Kepa credit, it was a sharp save.

Gyokeres with more gallant work in the channels for Arsenal but he is lacking some support at times, perhaps Eze and Guimaraes can change that.

Here come a raft of changes. Guirassy and Karestas on for Dortmund, replacing Beier and Fabio Silva.

Triple sub from Arsenal: Eze, Guimaraes and Timber replace Tzolis, Lewis-Skelly and White.

Dortmund are preparing a double substitution but Arsenal have a corner. Whipped into the near post by Rice, and Konsa and Gabriel rather got in each other’s way.

The game is really good contest now, high level Champions League fare. Arsenal might need the win if they want a top-two finish.

Anton looks short of pace at the back for Dortmund, and Gyokeres streaks away from him down the left. Hincapie is the player found with the cut-back, and he tees up White for a shot that is always rising.

A flowing move but it ended at the feet of two defenders.

Arsenal in search of an instant response, withe Odegaard finding Gyokeres with a pass into feet inside the box. His shot was blocked, and then Kobel saved Hincapie’s follow up header.

Madueke is then away from the right, shrugging off Anton, but no red shirt arrives in the six-yard box to reach his cross.

Arteta has been agitated since the half-time break and he will not have been impressed by the defensive work of Tzolis there. The Greek winger allowed Gadou to burst away and then dived in ineffectively as he ran downfield. These are the details and duels that Arteta obsesses over.

Goudou with a burst away from Tzolis and straight through the middle of the Arsenal midfield, and Beier’s first touch inside Gabriel was fantastic before he finished with a left-footed shot into the bottom corner. A very well-worked equaliser.

That’s how to break the Arsenal press. Run hard at Tzolis and give it everything. Great finish from Beier but an even better run from Joane Gadou to make it.

Maximilian Beier punishes Arsenal to make it 1-1 😳 https://t.co/OOUmg9JnHo

Kepa saves a routine shot from distance but almost puts Arsenal in trouble with his throw out, and there was an almighty 50:50 between Lewis-Skelly and Nmecha. At the other end, Odegaard neglected to shoot on his right foot after he was teed up by Madueke.

Looking back at the penalty shout, Gyokeres’ arm was slightly away from his body.

Dortmund’s best move and opportunity of the game, Svensson with a low cross that beats Konsa and Beier was in front of Gabriel but he completely missed an attempted flick at the near post.

Arsenal kick off the second 45 minutes. No changes from Arteta or Kovac.

A 70mph strike from Viktor Gyökeres against Dortmund 💨😮‍💨 https://t.co/hQHcCWvjUz

Noni Madueke has started nine of Arsenal's last 11 matches in all competitions. This run of games has had such a positive effect on him. He looks more confident, relaxed and expressive than at any point in his #AFC career. Perhaps not having the pressure of Saka has helped him.

Dortmund’s gameplan clearly based on the build-up from goalkeeper to the two centre-halves and then forward. It is a different prospect doing it in the Bundesliga to doing it against the Arsenal pressing machine and over the course of the first half Dortmund have lost their nerve in that regards. Goalkeeper Gregor Kobel has gone long to the left flank more than he would have liked. But – and it’s a significant point – they have looked quite good once they have got into Arsenal’s half. The Gyokeres goal was a good dig that beat Kobel with the dip. It was close to him. For all that Gyokeres was invited to shoot. Not a yellow shirt near by.

Arsenal much the better team across the 45 minutes, racking up 14 shots and enjoying 61 per cent possession. A familiar tale though, is their failure to convert that dominance into a commanding lead. Borussia Dortmund gradually carried more threat as the half progressed, and Arsenal cannot count on the insurance policy of Raya in goal. They need the second goal.

A moment of sloppiness from Arsenal near the end of the half, and Kepa was almost caught out at his near post but managed to make the save at the expense of a corner. Nmecha won first contact, but his header looped over.

Madueke wins the ball back high for Arsenal and finds Odegaard, but the flag goes up for offside against Arsenal’s captain. Replays suggest it was close, but Gyokeres was pleased to see the flag after missing a good chance in the middle.

Kepa patient on the ball for Arsenal to find Gabriel, who picks out Madueke with a diagonal over the top. Good close control from the winger, and he tees up Gyokeres for another attempt from just outside the box but he skies this one.

Dortmund win a corner from another Ryerson cross, he has looked their best outlet down the right. From the corner, Kepa was scrambling among bodies but Arsenal get away with it. Arteta wanted a foul on the goalkeeper.

Dortmund are a far more open opponent than Arsenal are used to facing in the Premier League, and they are fortunate not to have conceded more goals here, but they are willing to attack quite quickly in numbers. They’ve had five shots so far, and a couple of those were decent chances.

From the second phase of the next corner, Tzolis volleyed miles over when a shot was not on. Lewis-Skelly has been quietly effective in midfield for Arsenal, and there is applause for Ethan Nwaneri as he goes out to warm up for Dortmund. William Saliba is also out there stretching.

Incisive from Odegaard after Dortmund lost the ball in a dangerous position, and Rice charged straight through the middle, but was running out of steam as he took the shot and it deflected wide.

Corner taken short, well-worked between Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis, and the caught back falls for Gyokeres whose shot deflects wide for another corner.

No doubt Arsenal’s electric start of the opening 15 minutes has slowed, I’m not sure it would be possible or desirable to maintain that intensity across the 90 minutes. They are controlling the pace of and remaining patient, before Rice lets fly from almost 30 yards. Not far over the bar.

Dortmund with a nifty up, set and through but they had run offside. Gabriel then looks over the top for Hincapie, who was running over the top like a striker from left-back yet again.

Declan Rice with a crunching tackle in his own half that has the Emirates crowd on its feet, and Arsenal are flowing forward into space again but Gyokeres failed to pick the right final ball.

Now Dortmund have a corner after a Svensson shot deflects wide. Kepa claims with ease.

Hincapie, as we have seen with Arsenal’s full-backs all season, is popping up in advanced positions and he had a clear sight of goal but elected to pull the ball back when he should have put his laces through it. Well worked attack before then though, with Rice finding Odegaard between the lines and Gyokeres flicking the ball around the corner.

Better again from Dortmund, moving the ball with fluency from their own defensive third but Nmecha miscues his shot over the bar from the edge of the box. Kepa is then off his line to collect a chipped ball over the top.

Tzolis did well to harry and win the race to a long ball forward and he was close to flicking the ball into the path of Gyokeres.

Dortmund are starting to string some passes together, and they have a corner. This is one department where Arsenal will be appreciably worse without Raya but Hincapie heads clear.

Madueke then spins into space on the break and Gyokeres is free in the middle, but the winger slices the chipped pass.

Dortmund with their first attempt of the night after Ryerson swung in a cross from the left. Lewis-Skelly did well to compete in the air with Bellingham, before Silva kicked fresh air. Then with his second attempt, he volleyed over the bar.

Dortmund trying to settle into a spell of possession, but every pass feels like a chore for them at the moment and they are caught offside. Arsenal’s task now is to score the second while they have Dortmund where they want them. The German side will surely have a spell.

Gyokeres with another stretching run beyond Schlotterbeck, who is not the quickest. Arsenal completely dominant at the moment, but they do not always capitalise on these spells.

Chance for a second! Tzolis’ shot was parried by Kobel and Madueke’s rebound was blocked after he took a beat to control the ball. Could Madueke taken a swing first time?

Arsenal are well worth that opening goal. Looking back at the replays of Gyokeres’s strike, it was an unusual technique, brushing the turf before the ball much as a golfer might do with a bunker shot.

Gyokeres may lack craft at times but there is no doubt he has power. That was a superb strike, dipping towards goal with real ferocity. Arsenal don’t score many goals from range but they have plenty of players who can do it. Gyokeres now has five goals and three assists in his last 10 games for club and country.

Madueke in acres of space down the right again, and there was too much space in front of the Dortmund back three for Gyokeres to receive the ball and turn. From there, Gyokeres decided to take the shot on and his laces technique produced power and dip which deceived the goalkeeper Kobel. It was not in the corner, but the loop did for him. You can see Jobe is developing very well. As you also saw, he is now part of the England national team now.

I’m very impressed with them, with what Niko has done with the team, especially the way they are playing, the way they are dominating games, the amount of threat that they are able to create.

We had them here in pre-season (a 3-2 defeat) and they showed their quality and what they are capable of, so we are very much aware of that.

But we play at home in front of our crowd and we’re going to go and attack the game, that’s for sure.

Mikel Arteta seems quite set on his left-back pecking order: Riccardo Calafiori starts on weekends, and Piero Hincapie starts in midweek. They are very different players (Calafiori is the more adventurous, while Hincapie is more of an old-school defender) and it seems that Arteta feels Hincapie is better suited to Champions League football. He’ll be tested tonight against the Bundesliga leaders.

By Yannick HuberOn Tuesday, all eyes will be on Ethan Nwaneri. The Champions League clash between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund marks the 19-year-old’s return to the club where he grew up, where he became the Premier League’s youngest player and from whom he joined Dortmund on loan in the summer. It would be hard to imagine a more poignant setting. But for Nwaneri, facing Arsenal is about more than a reunion. It is also an opportunity to finally make his mark at Dortmund.

So far his time in Germany has not gone according to plan. Nwaneri arrived with a considerable reputation and high expectations, but has become less prominent in recent weeks. His playing time has diminished and he has frequently had to settle for a place on the bench.

But there are several reasons to believe that, of all games, this meeting with his former club could give his Dortmund career fresh impetus.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Rice, Lewis-Skelly; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; GyokeresSubs: Meslier, Porter, Saliba, Mosquera, Eze, Timber, Merino, Havertz, Calafiori, Guimaraes, Dowman

Dortmund: Kobel, Ryerson, Anton, Schlotterbeck, Gadou, Svensson, Veerman, Nmecha, Bellingham, Beier, SilvaSubs: Drewes, Meyer, Bensebaini, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Nwaneri, Karetsas, Sabitzer, Mane, Albert, Dos Santos, Reggiani

Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player the last time they played Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, and tonight he will have to make do without first-choice goalkeeper David Raya.

Arsenal’s manager struck an upbeat note when describing the shoulder or upper arm injury Raya sustained at Newcastle, and it appears he has avoided a long-term absence.

Even two weeks out, however, would mean Raya missing Premier League fixtures against Manchester City, Brentford and Spurs – possibly Arsenal’s most testing week of the season. Arteta did not rule out a return to face City on Sunday.

Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to deputise against Dortmund, who are top of the Bundesliga and have won three of their four Champions League league phase games. They won at the Emirates in a pre-season friendly, and Jobe Bellingham and on-loan Arsenal attacker Ethan Nwaneri are among their ranks.

These Champions League fixtures can feel secondary in importance to Premier League fare because of the competition’s new format, but a top-two finish in the league phase is a serious incentive.

As Arsenal discovered to their benefit last season when they “won” the league phase, the top two teams are rewarded with home second legs all the way to the final.

Arsenal are currently third on 10 points and face Real Madrid at the Emirates next, the team above them in second, so victory this evening is essential to set up that occasion.

Arteta has tended to make between four and six changes for these games, and Ben White, Piero Hincapie, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres are players pushing for starts after starting on the bench at Newcastle.

Also among the substitutes at St James’ Park was William Saliba, who is stepping up his return from a long-term back injury and could play his first minutes of the season tonight.

Willian had a long wait to get his move to Chelsea in 2013 and kept crossing paths with them along the way

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Willian has revealed how Chelsea tried to sign him months before he scored twice against them in the Champions League – and recalled the eyebrow-raising gift he received from a Blues supporter after the game.

The Brazilian winger joined Shakhtar Donetsk from Corinthians in 2007, aged just 19, but admits that he initially had reservations about moving to Ukraine.

Five years later, Chelsea were attempting to bring him to Stamford Bridge. Their January 2012 bid was rejected - but Willian went on to compel them to try again by scoring twice against the Blues in a dramatic 3-2 Champions League defeat that November.

Willian told FourFourTwo: "It wasn't easy. At that time, going straight to Ukraine was not my main goal. I think that every player, especially at that time, who dreamed of going to Europe, wanted to go to Italy or Spain."

"When this offer from Shakhtar came, my family and I talked about it and thought long and hard about whether to accept it. At first, we refused.

"But they kept insisting that I should at least go there to visit the club, visit the city, and learn more about their project. I ended up agreeing."

"I spent a few days there, and I liked what I saw, including the club's structure. There were already other Brazilians playing there too. That certainly made it easier for me to accept the offer.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"I remember that months before that game, Chelsea had already made an offer for me.

"he game was in November and their offer came in January 2012 - but Shakhtar didn't want to let me go."

"So, in the end, I stayed at Shakhtar and kept trying to leave. Then, in the group stage, I ended up scoring two goals at Stamford Bridge, so it was special.

"There's something funny about that day: after the match, a fan gave me a Chelsea shirt with my name on it and a question mark in place of the number. As if to say, 'what number will he wear when he plays here?'

"I thought it was funny and even took a photo holding that shirt!"

That supporter would eventually get their wish, in a roundabout way: Willian left Shakhtar for Anzhi Makhachkala in January 2013 before finally completing his move to Chelsea that August.

If Newcastle don't sign a Bruno Guimaraes replacement in January they could find themselves dragged into a relegation dogfight

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Watch Newcastle in their current, post-Bruno Guimaraes iteration and the same problem jumps off the screen. The energy is still there, and St James’ Park can still generate an intimidating atmosphere, but unless the team go direct, things slow to a crawl when the ball reaches midfield.

Losing Guimaraes was always going to leave a dent in the armoury, but the extent to which Newcastle have lost their forward punch is worrying from a black-and-white perspective. And the underlying numbers confirm what supporters were worried about.

According to Gradient Sports data, Newcastle have completed the fifth-lowest number of line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season.

Guimaraes lived for disguising passes through narrow gaps, taking two or three opponents out of the game with a single touch.

Without him, Newcastle’s midfield is a creativity bottleneck. They currently post the lowest completion rate for 'midfield line-breaking passes' across the entire division. Instead of playing forward, the ball gets stuck under players' feet, the tempo dies, and opposition defences are given plenty of time to shuffle across and set their shape.

Not a single Newcastle player sits inside the top 38 line-breaking passers in the Premier League this campaign, as per Gradient data.

Nico Gonzalez is the closest they have, coming in at 39th. He's tidy enough on the ball and offers some progression, but the data shows he is only a partial answer.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Gonzalez has attempted just four passes designed to break multiple lines all season, finding his man with only one of them. His numbers against the opposition's back four are similarly modest, having completed just one defensive line-breaking pass from three attempts. He keeps things ticking, but he isn't slicing teams open.

That hesitation in the middle is costing Newcastle badly further up the pitch. In Will Osula and Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Matthias Jaissle has two forwards who are quick off the mark and desperate to stretch games by spinning in behind.

Both players thrive on early, vertical service into space but at the moment, they are making the runs only to watch the ball get recycled sideways back towards the centre-halves. Until someone behind them starts making those aggressive passes, Newcastle are leaving weapons unused.

Nico Gonzalez - Newcastle - 2026/27 Premier League

Sporting director Ross Wilson doesn't need to break the bank to sort it out this winter, either. In France, Lorient’s Arthur Avom has quietly been putting up the exact numbers Newcastle are crying out for.

The 21-year-old Cameroon international is decisive and remarkably accurate. Compare his output directly with Newcastle's current midfielders and the difference is night and day.

Avom has completed three out of three multiple line-breaking passes this season, alongside seven from 10 when attempting to thread balls through the opposition’s defensive line. Just as eye-catching is his overall efficiency because Avom has completed 90 per cent of his line-breaking passes so far this campaign - the same ratio managed by Barcelona's former Ballon d'Or winner, Rodri.

Granted, Avom is playing in Ligue 1, not the Premier League or LaLiga, but matching the gold standard of European holding midfielders for progression in any division is no small feat.

Avom won't cost a fortune as his contract at Lorient expires at the end of the season, putting the French club in a weak negotiating position ahead of the January window.

Even if Lorient hold an undisclosed option to extend his deal by a further year, a winter fee would be comfortably within reach. Guimaraes can never be replaced like-for-like, of course, but if Newcastle want their attack firing again, bringing in Avom - or a player of his ilk - is a no-brainer.

#916. Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows

Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a new study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

Emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change. While over the past decade, these emissions have risen by 0.9% per year, they are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026.

"It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," said the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.

"So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons."

The study was released while global leaders are meeting in Turkey for the United Nations' COP31 climate conference.

The study published by international research group the Global Carbon Project found that oil emissions dropped by 1.9% in 2026, while natural gas fell by 0.3%. Coal emissions however continued to rise, by around 0.6%.

"A drop in emissions in ‌one year is not a peak unless it ‌is driven ​by structural change," Peters cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

A structural change would mean that emissions would slowly rise to a peak and then slowly decline afterward, indicating a long term trend. That's not what happened though, Peters said. "What we see this year is [that] oil emissions are going up and then suddenly, bang, down 2%."

It is the third time in recent years that global carbon pollution has dropped. The previous declines were during the global economic crisis in 2009 and during the COVID pandemic in 2020. In each of those cases, emissions went back up once global economies recovered.

While the geopolitical shocks of the past year have been the driving factors behind the temporary emissions reversal, there has also been a rise in renewable energy contributing to the data. So while solar panels, wind farms and electric vehicles did make a difference, they were just not enough to cut emissions by themselves.

"The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies," according to co-author of the study, Pierre Friedlingstein, of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University.

And even though emissions from fossil fuels dropped slightly, overall global carbon dioxide emissions still went up by about 1%, the study warns. The overall rise is because of land use changes like deforestation and peat fires, which increased too fast to be offset by the slight decrease in fossil fuel burning.

Enzo Maresca had two home games in four days to get Manchester City into decent shape for Sunday’s clash against Arsenal, which now feels like a must-win. On Tuesday, however, they ended up being taunted by Rasmus Hojlund on another evening that raised more questions than answers.

Olivera was taking a risk with that but was the contact enough to take Haaland down to the ground, that is the question?

The travelling Napoli fans are certainly making their voices heard inside the Etihad. They are currently making far more noise than the home supporters.

Enzo Maresca did confirm before the game that Cherki would start wide right and so that has proven. Brazilian forward Allan is out on the left with Fernandez playing in the ten role behind Haaland.

Should O’Reilly have done better with that chance? Nunes clips in a first-time cross from the right which picks out O’Reilly, whose header from eight yards out misses the target.

That was a nervy moment for Man City. Napoli captain Politano clips in a dangerous free-kick from the left to the back post, where McTominay tries to get on the end of it. However, Anderson gets a touch on it before the last touch comes off McTominay. Initially, a corner was given but that is overturned with McTominay touching it last.

Moments later, McTominay has a shot blocked from the left side of the box which goes behind for a corner. De Bruyne, who receives some applause as he goes over to take it, sends the corner too far and the ball goes behind for a goal kick.

The first corner of the night goes the way of the hosts as Anderson’s cross from the right is blocked by Olivera and spins behind for a corner. Interestingly, Napoli have left three players up the pitch.

Man City take it short, with Anderson and Fernandez working it well before the latter has a shot blocked inside the Napoli penalty area.

You would not call Napoli a side in form. Max Allegri’s men have just six wins from 16 games in the league and Champions League so far this season. Manchester City have failed to win any of their last four league games but have won three from four in this competition.

The first chance of the night goes the way of the hosts. Anderson shoots from range and forces Napoli keeper Milinkovic-Savic into a fairly routine save down to his right. Anderson scored a good goal at the weekend in Man City’s draw against Fulham but that effort did not have enough power on it to trouble the Napoli keeper.

Khaldoon Al-Mubarak is here, sat next to Uefa president Aleksander Čeferin.....

After Kevin De Bruyne exchanges plenty of hugs with some former teammates, both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off at the Etihad. A banner for De Bruyne is unveiled. There are a lot of empty seats at the Etihad this evening. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Manchester City: Donnarumma; Nunes, Guéhi, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Bouaddi, Anderson; Cherki, Fernandez, Allan; Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Ndiaye, Kovačić, Doku, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Khusanov, Foden, McAidoo, Samba, Lewis.

Napoli: Milinković-Savić; Beukema, Rrahmani, Olivera; Politano, De Bruyne, Gilmour, McTominay, Spinazzola; Lang; Højlund.Substitutes: Chiummariello, Contini, Lucca, Neres, Giovane, Spinelli, Anguissa.

City will be wearing an orange kit tonight, a special edition in collaboration with fashion brand CP Company. Napoli are also wearing away colours so it will not look much like City v Napoli when they players head out of the tunnel.

How much are Man City missing Kevin De Bruyne? 🤔 Joleon Lescott gives his verdict 👀 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/pogjeOi00P

It is not just Kevin De Bruyne in this Napoli side who is used to the Premier League. In total, there are four former Premier League players in their starting XI; De Bruyne, Rasmus Hojlund, Billy Gilmour and Scott McTominay. On the bench is then former Fulham midfielder André-Frank Zambo Anguissa.

Napoli appear depleted. They have only named seven subs and two of those are goalkeepers. But their midfield has a familiar Premier League look to it with Kevin De Bruyne starting alongside Billy Gilmour and Scott McTominay.

Aston Villa have made the trip out to Istanbul to face Galatasaray and are currently 1-0 down. You can follow the closing stages to that match right here.

Meanwhile in north London, Arsenal host Borussia Dortmund, with that game kicking off at 8pm.

“I am proud of what I have done as a football player, and honestly, this is my club, I love the owners. I have even spoken to [chairman] Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] about how to buy a club. I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change, [the way] the people treated me and my family for 10 years.

“Of course, in life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit. I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That is the thing that I value most. I have given my all and that is not going to change in my mind. I do not think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played. But everybody has their own opinion, I guess. Other people may be ‘disgraced’ a bit, but I cannot change anything about that.”

Kevin De Bruyne has been lined up for a January move to PSV Eindhoven, with the Dutch club working on a deal to land one of the Premier League’s greatest players when the window opens.

De Bruyne, 35, has been at Napoli since the start of last season but it is understood that a move away from the Serie A club is now on the horizon. He is still under contract at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona so PSV will pay a fee to land him as they look to retain their Eredivisie title.

At Manchester City, De Bruyne won six Premier League titles and was part of their Treble-winning team that won the Champions League. During the last 18 months at Napoli he has suffered injury issues, had a row with team-mate on the pitch and was quoted as saying he was glad Antonio Conte left as head coach.

“Not a lot I can say for the moment,” said De Bruyne when asked about his future. “I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36.

“There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening.”

It is matchday five of the Champions League as Manchester City host Napoli at the Etihad. These sides last met back in September 2025, with Manchester City winning 2-0 at home courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku. Manchester City’s cause was helped by an early red card for Napoli’s Giovanni Di Lorenzo. Napoli’s only win over Manchester City came all the way back in November 2011 when they won 2-1 after a double from Edinson Cavani.

Manchester City have won three of their opening four Champions League matches this season, with their only defeat coming at home against back-to-back champions PSG. They drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday, which means they are now without a league win in four games.

“We are always looking to win games, no matter the competition,” Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca said. “For sure, the four games in a row in the Premier League that we did not win has been a shame. Tomorrow [tonight] we have a chance to win the game and continue our path in the Champions League that at the moment has been very good. First of all, it is important to qualify and then probably, if you are not able to finish in the top eight, you have two more games that with the amount of games that we have, it is always important to reduce games. So the target is to try and finish in the top eight.”

Napoli, managed by Massimiliano Allegri, have struggled thus far in this season’s Champions League, winning just one of their opening four games and are all the way down in 27th. They come into tonight’s match off the back of a 1-0 home win over Torino in Serie A on the weekend courtesy of former Manchester United midfielder Scott McTominay’s winning goal. However, they still sit down in eighth in the Italian top flight, a massive 14 points off the top through just 12 games.

“This match will not be decisive,” Allegri said. “It is a simple mathematical equation, but obviously we will try to do well, even against a great team like Manchester City. It will be a beautiful and fascinating challenge and we want to play to the best of our ability. Ultimately, our goal is to qualify. We must not repeat the mistakes we made in Porto, where we played a great game for 70 minutes and then let ourselves go, conceding chances too easily. We will have to be able to play both with and without possession.”

Team news from the Etihad to follow shortly.

Chantelle Cameron, the unified super-welterweight world champion, has agreed a multi-fight extension with Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions.

The reigning WBO, WBA and WBC super-welterweight world titlist is one of the world's top pound-for-pound fighters.

The new agreement extends MVP's partnership with Cameron following a landmark 2026 campaign that saw the English fighter capture world championships in a second weight division - further cementing her position among boxing's elite - and beat American star Mikaela Mayer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

A former undisputed super-lightweight world champion, and the only professional opponent to beat Katie Taylor, Cameron will continue pursuing the biggest fights in women's boxing, starting with her rematch with Mayer on December 24.

Nakisa Bidarian and Paul, founders of Most Valuable Promotions, said: "Chantelle Cameron has established herself as one of the true GOATs of women's boxing and what makes her special is that she's still hungry for more.

"Look at her resume and it is clear she is the pound-for-pound No 1 fighter in the world. In just over a year with MVP, she's unified three world titles at 154 pounds, headlined a major event in her home country, and is now preparing for another massive championship fight on Christmas Eve in Dubai as part of one of the biggest combat sports events of 2026.

"Chantelle has made it clear that she wants to keep challenging herself against the toughest competition, and we're committed to delivering those fights. This extension is about building on everything we've accomplished together and making sure the next chapter of her career is even bigger."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Cameron said: "I'm delighted to extend my contract with MVP. Since I first signed with Nakisa and Jake they have delivered on every single promise they made to me.

"They have looked after me in and out of the ring and signing a long-term extension was a very easy decision on my part.

"I am boxing on the biggest cards all over the world and I look forward to the rest of my career with MVP."

#911. Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health

More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

Some 50,000 deaths can be attributed to malnutrition in Germany each year, according to the German Society for Nutritional Medicine (DGEM).

The problem is that malnutrition often doesn't become apparent until the consequences are already severe.

"In most cases, you don't notice anything at first," said Matthias Pirlich, a nutritional expert and internal medicine specialist, who once served as DGEM vice president. "You could have a severe vitamin D deficiency for months before any symptoms appear at all. The same applies for vitamin B12. By the time symptoms appear, such as nerve damage, it's already too late."

A long-term B12 deficiency can damage the spinal cord, leading to numbness in the limbs, muscle weakness or even paralysis. Less common deficiency-related brain damage can cause memory loss and mental health issues.

All B vitamins play an important role in metabolism, blood formation and healthy nerve function.

Vitamins, along with various minerals such as calcium, magnesium, iron, iodine and zinc, are classed as micronutrients. The body needs to source them from food, as it cannot produce them itself. Our bodies also need macronutrients like carbohydrates, carbohydrates, protein and fats that provide us with energy.

If the body consumes less food than it needs to maintain all bodily functions over a prolonged period of time, then this is known as undernutrition. A recent World Food Organization (FAO) report estimates that approximately 645 million people worldwide suffer from chronic undernutrition.

Malnutrition, on the other hand, occurs when we consume enough calories but lack certain macronutrients or micronutrients in our food. This, too, can make one sick over time and even prove fatal. About 2 billion people worldwide suffer from this so-called hidden hunger, most of them in the Global South. That said, even some people in industrialized nations lack important micronutrients in their nutrition.

One study, for instance, found that just under three-quarters of the US population did not meet the recommended daily intake of vitamin D between 2007 and 2010, with more than two-thirds falling short of the recommended amount of vitamin E. And in Germany, about one-third of the population suffered from vitamin D deficiency in 2017, according to the German Nutrition Society. Such deficiency can cause bone, joint and muscle pain. It may also lead to an increased risk of falls and bone fractures.

About one-third of Germans also had an insufficient intake of iodine, a trace element that is indispensable for the production of thyroid hormones. Iodine deficiency can therefore disrupt normal thyroid function. Not only that — during pregnancy, a baby's brain and nervous system can only properly develop with an adequate supply of iodine.

The cultivation of agricultural produce with partially long shelf life or high yields has in some cases caused a decrease in the micronutrient content of fruits, vegetables and grains. Whether this drop in micronutrients is impacting human health, however, is a matter of debate.

Malnutrition can result from an unbalanced diet that, while filling and providing energy, lacks essential micronutrients. Examples of such empty calories include fast food and highly processed foods, as well as white bread and white rice.

Poverty is often the reason for such an unbalanced diet, for example when people in the Global South can only afford to buy staples such as flour or rice.

Another study found that in Germany, households at risk of poverty are more likely to consume foods that are low in nutrients and high in calories.

Depression is also associated with an increased risk of nutrient deficiency. "People often lose their appetite, and when they neglect their self-care, they may end up eating a very unbalanced diet," Pirlich told DW. His research shows that older adults and people who live alone often develop malnutrition, too. The risk also increases the more medications a person takes.

Many diseases result in the body being less efficient at absorbing or utilizing nutrients through the intestines. This applies to people with inflammatory or chronic disease, such as Crohn's disease, celiac disease, liver disease and cancer.

The DGEM estimates that some 30% of all patients receiving inpatient care in Germany are affected by or at risk of malnutrition. Yet health insurance data shows that only about 1% of patients are screened and treated for nutrient deficiencies.

Often, patients' malnutrition worsens during their hospital stay. The consequences can be serious, potentially causing additional complications, delayed recuperation, longer hospital stays and even increased mortality rates. This results in higher healthcare expenditure, amounting to billions each year.

German policymakers and medical associations are therefore developing a plan to better screen for and treat malnutrition in hospitals. The road map will be ready by 2027 and copy the Dutch approach in the sense that all patients are checked for nutritional deficiencies upon hospital admission.

Pirlich wants to see such screenings for at-risk groups in outpatient clinics, too: "This includes all those with chronic and serious illnesses and, above all, older adults."

To prevent poverty-related malnutrition, Pirlich suggests increased access to healthy food, offering free school meals as an example.

The nutritional expert recommends eating a diet that is varied and largely plant-based. "Secondary plant compounds have a very positive effect, and if you eat a highly diverse diet, you consume many different foods that are [nutritionally] beneficial," said Pirlich.

There's a simple rule of thumb: The more colorful your food, the better.

Also, cook vegetables as gently as possible, because overheating and keeping them warm for too long destroys their vitamins. Long storage periods also lead to vitamin loss, so it makes sense to go for seasonal and regional foods in particular.

But even when ensuring a healthy and balanced diet, some people still develop a nutrient deficiency. A blood test can provide clarity, and dietary supplements may help make up for the deficiency.

This article was originally written in German.

Manchester United have finalised their transfer strategy heading into the winter window.

The Red Devils are languishing in 19th place in the Premier League with just one win all season, in what's becoming their biggest crisis in the modern era.

With new manager Mauricio Pochettino at the wheel, however, plans are already in motion to improve the squad – with new arrivals coming to Old Trafford in January.

Manchester United were battered at the hands of Liverpool at the weekend in Pochettino's bow, which highlighted the problems across the team.

Leny Yoro was sent off early in the fixture, with Matthijs De Ligt criticised on his first Premier League start of the season, as Pochettino's men shipped four at Anfield.

Now, TEAMtalk have reported that United are prioritising a central defender, a left-back and a striker in January.

Calvin Bassey is high on the wish list – with the Fulham man left-footed – with the likes of Jarrad Branthwaite and Nathan Collins also on the radar.
